hub.title: Your first pull request starts here
hub.lede: Beginner-friendly issues from open-source projects with Algerian maintainers or a clear link to Algeria. Every listed project pledges to answer newcomers within 7 days.
hub.no_match: Try another language or label, or clear the filters.
hub.note: Open issues labelled {gfi} or {hw} in listed projects, refreshed from GitHub every {hours} hours. Each card links to the issue on GitHub.
hub.empty_title: The first projects are being listed.
hub.empty: Their beginner issues appear here as soon as they pass the seven listing checks. Maintain an open-source project with a link to Algeria? Listing it takes one pull request, and no account.
hub.step1: Comment on it to say you’re working on it, so nobody duplicates your work.
hub.step2_t: Open a draft pull request early
hub.step2: Push a first version and ask questions in the pull request. Small is fine.
hub.step3: Listed maintainers pledge to review or answer newcomers within a week.
hub.projects_lede: Every listed project passes a daily health check: recent commits, open beginner issues and the djazairdev topic. Dashed cards are projects Algeria’s ecosystem still needs.
hub.projects_note: A project that fails a check for 14 days is hidden until it’s fixed, and one that removes the topic leaves at once. {report}.

divisions.title: Administrative divisions as open data
divisions.text: Wilayas and communes after the April 2026 reorganisation, with official codes, under an open licence.

payments.title: Payment software kits
payments.text: Open SDKs for Algerian payment gateways, with tests and examples. Maintain one? List it.

languages.title: Darija and Tamazight language tools
languages.text: Tokenisers, spell-checkers and open datasets for languages spoken in Algeria.

hub.list_lede: Add one entry to projects.yml, or fill in the issue form if you’d rather not use git. No djazair.dev account needed: the djazairdev topic proves you maintain the repository.

check.activity: At least one commit in the last 90 days
check.docs: A README and a CONTRIBUTING file
check.issues: At least 3 open issues labelled {gfi} or {hw}
check.pledge: Maintainers pledge to reply to newcomer pull requests within 7 days
check.topic: The repository carries the GitHub topic {topic}
check.relevance: Algerian maintainers, or clear relevance to Algeria

hub.check_note: A failing check names what to fix. A code of conduct is recommended, not required.
hub.list_note: Submissions are reviewed in public within 7 days. Language, licence and activity are read from GitHub, so the entry stays short.

checks.when: Runs on every submission and daily after listing

orgs.title: Organisations per account

topics.title: Topics above GitHub’s threshold

doesnt: The share of people who code

trends.title: How the numbers moved since {year}
trends.lede: Quarterly series from GitHub’s Innovation Graph. Pick an indicator, index everything to the start of {year}, or bring one peer forward. Hover, drag or use the arrow keys to read exact values.
trends.summary: Line chart of {indicator} from {from} to {to} for Algeria, the North African median and six peers. Algeria in {last}: {value}.
trends.summary_indexed: Line chart of {indicator}, indexed to {quarter} = 100, from {from} to {to} for Algeria, the North African median and six peers. Algeria in {last}: {value}.
trends.readout: Chart readout. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between quarters, and Home and End for the first and last.
trends.source: Source: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0), {from} – {to}. N. Africa median of {members}.
trends.fig2_title: Developer accounts, growth from Q{n} to Q{n}
trends.fig2_lede_dip: Growth slowed from {first} in {y0} to {low} in {ylow}, then jumped to {last} in {yn}, the fastest pace in the series.
trends.fig2_lede: Growth went from {first} in {y0} to {last} in {yn}. The fastest pace was {high} in {yhigh}, the slowest {low} in {ylow}.
trends.fig2_summary: Bar chart of year-on-year growth in developer accounts, each Q{n} compared with Q{n} a year earlier, from {y0} to {yn}. {yn}: {last}.
trends.fig2_source: Source: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0). Comparing Q{n} with Q{n} removes seasonal swings.
trends.why_index_text: Indexing sets every economy to 100 at the start of {year}, so the lines compare growth, not size. In {last}, Algeria stands at {dz}: {times} times its level in {first}. {peer} stands at {peer_value}, the highest of the six peers.
trends.why_median: Why a median, not an average?
trends.why_median_text: Seven economies is a small group. One large value, like {country}’s {value} accounts, would pull an average up. The median is the middle value, so one outlier can’t move it far.
trends.table_caption: {title}: Algeria, the North African median and six peers, by quarter
trends.table_note: The table follows the indicator and scale selected above. Every figure is also in the CSV.

peers.title: Algeria and its peers, {quarter}
peers.lede: Algeria next to three groups: six core peers, the seven North African economies, and Africa’s {n} largest developer communities. In the rank tables, each figure shows its place in the group, where 1 is the highest.
peers.core_lede: Morocco, Tunisia and Egypt are Algeria’s North African neighbours with large developer communities; Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa are Africa’s largest. The last rows give each group’s median.
peers.na_lede: All seven, whatever their size. Sort any column to see where Algeria falls.
peers.af_lede: Every African economy with at least {min} developer accounts a year earlier: {n} in {quarter}. The minimum size keeps the swings of small communities out of the ranking.
peers.caption: {group}, {quarter}: each figure with its rank in the group
peers.source: Source: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0), {quarter} · World Bank population, {year}. Rank 1 is the highest; ties share a place.

languages.title: Languages in Algeria, {quarter}
languages.lede: The ten languages the most developers in Algeria pushed code in during the quarter, and how that changed in a year. One developer can push in several languages, so the counts can’t be added up.
languages.fig_summary: Developers in Algeria who pushed in each of the ten most used languages in {quarter}: those a year earlier, and those added since.
languages.lede_lead_always: {lang} is first, as in every quarter since {first}.
languages.lede_new: {new} entered the top ten, in place of {out}.
languages.lede_fast: {lang} grew fastest: {pct} on a year earlier.
languages.source: Source: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0), {quarter}. Developers who pushed in each language during the quarter.
languages.rw_add: The counts can’t be added up
languages.rw_add_text: One developer can push in several languages in a quarter: someone who writes HTML, CSS and JavaScript counts in all three. The ten counts come to {sum}, which counts many developers more than once.
languages.rw_markup_text: GitHub detects languages from the files pushed, so markup such as HTML and CSS, Jupyter notebooks and files such as Dockerfile count too.
languages.rw_threshold_text: GitHub lists a language for an economy only when 100 or more developers push in it. In {quarter}, {n} languages pass that in Algeria.

languages.peers_lede: The three languages with the most developers pushing in each economy, and how many languages pass GitHub’s threshold of 100 developers.

languages.peers_source: Source: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0), {quarter}. A language is listed once 100 or more developers push in it.

about.title: About djazair.dev
about.lede: An open scorecard of Algeria’s developer ecosystem and a hub for its open-source projects, built in the open.
about.analytics_on: We count visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies and doesn’t follow you from site to site: it keeps totals only, such as pages viewed, countries and browsers.

downloads.title: Data and downloads
downloads.lede: Every table behind the Index as CSV and JSON, free to reuse under CC0. Each quarter’s files stay online with a manifest of checksums, and every change is logged.
downloads.tables_lede: The {n} tables of the {quarter} data, computed from GitHub Innovation Graph release {release}. The data dictionary describes every column.
downloads.checksums: The manifest lists every file with its size and SHA-256 checksum, so you can check what you downloaded.
downloads.earlier_none: {quarter} is the first quarter published. Earlier quarters will stay online, unchanged, as new ones arrive.
downloads.charts_lede: The figures behind every chart on the site, as CSV and JSON. Each chart’s download menu also has SVG and PNG files, dark or light.
downloads.addresses_lede: Stable addresses, served with CORS, so code and pages on other sites can fetch them. latest.json names the newest quarter’s folder; a folder never changes once a newer quarter is out.
downloads.changelog_lede: One entry per data release, with any revised past values flagged, and the changes to the site worth knowing about.
downloads.corrections_lede: Every correction to a published number or statement, with the date the error was found and the date it was fixed. Corrections are published within 7 days of discovery.
downloads.licence_lede: The derived data is CC0 1.0: use it for anything, without asking. Credit is welcome, not required. Accounts per million people also uses World Bank population, which is CC BY 4.0: when you reuse that column, credit the World Bank. Text and charts on the site are CC BY 4.0.
downloads.attribution_text: Data: GitHub Innovation Graph (CC0) · djazair.dev. Population: World Bank (CC BY 4.0).
downloads.attribution_note: Population figures are the World Bank’s for {year}.

reports.lede: A short report on each quarter’s data, in Arabic and English: the headline numbers, what changed, how Algeria compares with its peers, one subject in depth, and what the numbers can’t tell you.
reports.schedule: Within 14 days of each data release
reports.next: The next report covers the next quarter’s data and follows GitHub’s next release.
reports.none: The first report is being written.

rule.accounts_text: The data counts accounts, dormant ones included, so headlines say “developer accounts”.
rule.bad_news: Bad news as clearly as good
rule.bad_news_text: A fall gets the same space and the same plain words as a rise.
rule.medians_text: Algeria is compared with the median of each peer group rather than with one neighbour.
rule.checked_text: Before a report is published, someone other than its author checks every number against the published data, and a fluent reader checks each translation.
rule.corrections_text: Mistakes are fixed and listed in the corrections log within 7 days of being found. We never credit GitHub with a claim it didn’t make.
